plants.name: Prunus campanulata
plants.description: Before most trees have stirred, this cherry covers its bare branches in nodding, bell-shaped blossoms of deep rose-pink. The flowers hang in small clusters and glow against winter hillsides. They draw flocks of bulbuls and white-eyes that come to sip nectar.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late January to February, with the peak varying by elevation
plants.funFact: Okinawa's cherry blossom season is the earliest in Japan. It begins in January, weeks before the famous cherry blooms of the mainland.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs burst into rose-like blooms with layers of silky petals and a boss of golden stamens. Against dark green leaves, the flowers look almost sculpted. They brighten gardens in the depths of winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter to early spring, from about December through March in mild climates
plants.location: Gardens of the Pacific Northwest and southern United States, western Europe, and Japan
plants.funFact: Camellia sinensis, a close relative, produces the leaves used to make all true tea.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: Rounded umbels of trumpet-shaped flowers rise on tall, slender stems above arching, strap-like leaves. In the Southern Hemisphere summer, they put on a show in blue and violet. They are a staple of coastal gardens and roadsides.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer, roughly December through February
plants.location: Eastern South Africa, and gardens in Australia and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Despite the common name, agapanthus is not a true lily. The name comes from Greek words meaning 'love flower'.
